sam-darnold.name: Sam Darnold
sam-darnold.bio:
Sam Darnold entered the NFL as the No. 3 overall pick in the 2018 draft by the New York Jets after a decorated run at USC, where he helped lead the Trojans to a Rose Bowl victory and earned Offensive MVP honors in the 2017 game with five touchdown passes and 473 total yards. He spent his first three professional seasons with the Jets before moving to the Carolina Panthers in 2021 and 2022, then had one-season stops with the San Francisco 49ers in 2023 and the Minnesota Vikings in 2024. Over that stretch, he settled into a long career marked by regular starting opportunities and steady volume, entering Seattle with 100 games played and 90 starts.

Darnold’s one season in Minnesota became a turning point. In 2024, he started all 17 games and produced career-best totals in passing yards, touchdowns, and passer rating, completing 361 of 545 passes for 4,319 yards, 35 touchdowns, and 12 interceptions. That performance earned him Pro Bowl recognition and led into his move to Seattle, where he signed as an unrestricted free agent on March 13, 2025.

His first season with the Seahawks was his most productive yet. Darnold started every game in 2025, throwing for 4,048 yards and 25 touchdowns while completing 67.7 percent of his passes and posting a 99.1 passer rating. Seattle went 14-3, won the NFC West, secured the NFC’s No. 1 seed, and set a franchise record for regular-season wins. In the postseason, he directed the Seahawks past the Rams in the NFC Championship with 346 passing yards and three touchdowns, then helped Seattle defeat New England in Super Bowl LX. He entered 2026 as Seattle’s starting quarterback.
careerHighlights: No. 3 overall pick in the 2018 NFL draft
2017 Rose Bowl Offensive MVP at USC
Career-best 4,319 passing yards and 35 touchdowns in 2024
Pro Bowl selection in 2024 and 2025
Signed with the Seattle Seahawks as an unrestricted free agent in 2025
Started every game in Seattle’s 14-3 NFC West championship season
Threw for 346 yards and three touchdowns in the 2025 NFC Championship
sam-darnold.seasonOverview: Darnold’s latest listed season has been a brief start to 2026, with only one game and two passing attempts recorded. The small sample offers little to measure beyond his continued presence on Seattle’s roster after an accomplished first year with the Seahawks in 2025, when he anchored a 14-3 team that reached and won Super Bowl LX.

jaxon-smith-njigba.name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
jaxon-smith-njigba.bio:
Jaxon Smith-Njigba entered his fourth season with the Seattle Seahawks in 2026 after establishing himself as one of the franchise’s most productive receivers. His role grew quickly in Seattle, and by 2024 he had earned his first Pro Bowl selection after catching 100 passes for 1,130 yards. That production carried into a landmark 2025 season, when he finished with 119 receptions, 1,793 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns. He led the NFL in receiving yards, set Seahawks single-season records for both receptions and receiving yards, and was named AP Offensive Player of the Year and first-team All-Pro.

Smith-Njigba’s performance helped anchor a Seattle offense that finished 14-3 and went on to win Super Bowl LX in the 2025 season. The Seahawks followed that championship run by signing him to a multi-year contract extension on March 25, 2026, underscoring his place at the center of the team’s future. Through the early part of the 2026 season, he remained a focal point of the passing game, adding 8 receptions for 122 yards and a touchdown in the opening game.

A former Ohio State receiver, Smith-Njigba’s Seattle tenure has been defined by steady growth into high-volume production and league-wide recognition. His progression from strong contributor to record-setting centerpiece has made him one of the defining players of the Seahawks’ recent era.
